assessments.rationale: evd-002 and evd-003 describe the existence of the Transcript Exporter, Training Store, Tuning Job, and Reply Service, and that full transcripts (including personal data) are exported and used for training. They do not describe tenant models, access-enforced separation of stored artifacts by tenant, or how thr-001 is defined. On this documentation alone, it is not established that req-DATA-003 is out of scope for thr-001; the non-applicability conclusion rests on unstated threat and requirement definitions rather than on the cited passages.
missing_evidence: Threat model documentation for thr-001 describing the attack path and which storage locations are involved.
Design or policy documentation for req-DATA-003 that defines its scope and any tenant-level storage separation implemented for the Training Store and related artifacts.

assessments.rationale: The passages in evd-002 and evd-003 show that closed-ticket transcripts are exported in full to a Training Store and used for model training, with no redaction or filtering step. They do not mention any customer-initiated deletion procedures, how deletions propagate to training data, or how req-DATA-004 is scoped, nor do they define thr-001. The claim that customer-initiated deletion is not applicable to this poisoning threat is therefore not established by the cited documentation.

Architecture or data-lifecycle documentation explaining how customer-initiated deletions interact with the Training Store and fine-tuned model.
A detailed description of thr-001 to show whether deletion behavior could meaningfully mitigate it.

assessments.rationale: evd-002 states that there is a weekly Tuning Job that "fine-tunes the vendor's base reply model on the training store's current contents" and that the Transcript Exporter is the only writer to the Training Store with a dedicated job identity, while evd-003 confirms that what customers write is what the model trains on. evd-005 indicates that customers write the ticket messages that become training data. Together, these passages directly support that the system fine-tunes a model on collected data originating from many customers, so the applicability of a training-corpus control like req-TRAIN-001 to thr-001 is well supported. However, none of the evidence describes the specific control behaviors required by req-TRAIN-001 or demonstrates that those requirements are fully satisfied; the status "satisfied" is therefore not established by the documentation.
missing_evidence: Control or design documentation for req-TRAIN-001 describing the required governance of training-corpus write paths.

Configuration or implementation evidence showing how the Training Store's write path and associated identities implement all aspects of req-TRAIN-001, beyond the single-writer property described in evd-002.

assessments.rationale: evd-002 explains that transcripts exported to the Training Store include "customer names, email addresses, and complete message bodies," and evd-003 notes that there is no redaction or filtering and that what the customer wrote is what the model trains on. This directly supports that training data derives from user/customer production content, so the applicability of req-TRAIN-002 to thr-001 is well documented. However, the evidence does not describe any of the specific protections or controls that req-TRAIN-002 might require, and thus does not support the claim that the requirement is currently "partially_satisfied" rather than simply unknown. The satisfaction level portion of the conclusion is therefore not established.
missing_evidence: Definition of req-TRAIN-002 and its required controls for training on user/customer content.
Design or implementation documentation showing which of those controls are implemented for this Training Store and tuning process, to justify the "partially_satisfied" status.

assessments.rationale: evd-002 states that the Tuning Job "writes the tuned model artifact to the artifact bucket," and evd-004 further explains that the tuning job writes each week's artifact to the artifact bucket and that agents are served whichever artifact is most recent. This directly supports that tuned artifacts are both produced and served, so the applicability of req-TRAIN-003 to thr-001 is well supported. The evidence, however, does not describe any of the controls that req-TRAIN-003 might require around those artifacts, so the mapping's classification of the requirement as "unverified" is not grounded in the documents; the evidence simply does not speak to whether the requirement's control set is met or not.
missing_evidence: Definition of req-TRAIN-003 and the required controls around tuned model artifacts.
Configuration or design documentation for the artifact bucket and serving path showing how those controls are or are not implemented.
